messages:
sasha: FYI hitting a weird failure on a customer private deploy — their onprem agent can't finish the KMS TLS handshake and audit logs stopped showing up. Root started ~10:00 UTC.

emma: ugh. any recent RBAC changes on the agent SA?

sasha: we rolled a permissions cleanup yesterday (removed a broad clusterrole). suspect it might have removed the audit-log writer role binding to the service account. But TLS handshake failing makes me also think netpol/egress.

raj: can you paste the agent logs? short snippets ok.

sasha: 
```
2026-03-20T09:59:41Z error: tls handshake failed: remote error: handshake failure
2026-03-20T09:59:42Z warn: audit plugin: unable to emit event: permission denied
```

kim: those two together look like: agent tries to call KMS (client cert), KMS returns handshake fail (maybe proxy or wrong SNI), and agent can't write to audit sink in cluster. For private deployments we've seen failures when NetworkPolicy blocks egress to the KMS appliance IP or when a mutating webhook rewrites SA tokens.

matt: quick checks: 1) is the node able to resolve KMS fqdn? 2) are we forcing egress through an outbound proxy that needs allowlist?

sasha: nslookup and curl from a debug pod: 
```
# from debug-pod
> nslookup kms.customer.local
Name: kms.customer.local
Address: 10.131.8.44
> curl -vk https://kms.customer.local:443
* Connected to 10.131.8.44 port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake error
```

emma: ok DNS and connectivity fine. That rules out cloud DNS. Need to verify KMS logs — did they reject client cert or SA JWT?

raj: also check NetworkPolicy on the agent namespace — if they applied deny-egress: true it might allow tcp/443 only to a narrow list.

kim: on RBAC side, run: `kubectl get rolebinding -n agent-namespace -o yaml | grep audit-log` — if binding is gone, agent may now fail to write events (which we saw).

infra-bot: deploy status: private-agent/sha@20260320 rolled back automatically to previous revision at 10:03 UTC due to unhealthy readiness checks.

matt: mitigation plan: 1) rebind the audit-log-writer role to the agent SA (temp). 2) ask customer to allow egress to KMS IP and to the HSM-proxy on 443 with SNI preserved. 3) collect tcpdump to see TLS ClientHello SNI and certs.

sasha: starting step 1 now. will apply a temporary RoleBinding and push.

emma: pj: if RBAC rollback fixed audit writes but handshake still fails then it's definitely netpol/proxy.

raj: for tcpdump run on pod: `kubectl exec -it debug-pod -- tcpdump -n -s 0 -w - port 443` and capture first 20 packets, then share pcap with KMS team. note: ensure customer consent.

kim: also check if the service account token projection is being rotated by a webhook (we had a bug where mutating webhook replaced token path and broke mTLS cert fetch).

sasha: update: after re-adding RoleBinding audit-log-writer to agent SA audit events resumed (verified). but TLS handshake still failing.

matt: progress. that isolates it to network or KMS config. next steps: get tcpdump and the KMS server TLS logs. if KMS complains about unsupported TLS version or missing SNI we can correlate.

emma: one-off mitigation for customer: temporarily allow all egress from agent namespace to KMS IP to unblock traffic while we triage. we should document the change + expiry.

kim: long-term fix ideas: 1) add automated integration test for private deploys that validates egress rules to known KMS endpoints; 2) add a diagnostic probe that attempts a KMS handshake and fails open/alerts before agent flips into unhealthy; 3) ensure our RBAC cleanup playbook preserves audit bindings.

raj: vuln triage note: we flagged a CVE in an older openssl on HSM proxy last month. customer said they patched, but if patch changed negotiated cipher suites it might drop clients. ask KMS team to share cipher list.

sasha: we've got tcpdump pcap and sent to customer security + KMS team. awaiting their TLS server logs.

infra-bot: audit entry: incident 2026-03-20-priv-kms-egress created by sasha. Severity: P2.

sec-oncall: tagging for follow-up: create a playbook snippet for "private-deploy: if KMS handshake + audit silence" that includes RBAC check, netpol check, tcpdump commands, and temp mitigation. I'll take that action item.

matt: small config note for the playbook: include a command to check node egress SNAT: `kubectl -n agent-namespace exec -it debug-pod -- curl -sS https://ifconfig.me` and verify the source IP is allowlisted on the KMS side.

sasha: thanks all. will update once KMS team responds. :handshake:
